target_customer: Clinical researchers, diagnostics developers and biopharma teams that need to measure DNA methylation, especially from blood-based liquid biopsy samples
problem: Standard methylation workflows (bisulfite conversion and similar) damage DNA and limit sensitivity. Epinoma says its EpiAmp chemistry copies DNA while keeping methylation marks, so epigenetic signals can be read at lower detection limits.
business_model: Research tools and reagents, with a path to diagnostics and epigenetic therapeutics partnerships (company site: disease detection, programmable epigenetic therapies, biopharma partnering)

founders.name: Varun Govil
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a background in translational medicine and prior biotech and medtech development. Named as CEO on the Polsky Center article. Education and employers not listed in sources opened.

founders.name: Zhijian Li
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a background in chemistry and biomedical science and diagnostic and prognostic method development. COO title comes from an aggregator profile (unverified).

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires new enzyme and protein chemistry for methyl-preserving amplification, licensed from University of Chicago research (Chuan He lab), plus clinical validation. Research-grade for an eight-person team.

defensibility.rationale: Core technology rests on a university license and a patent application filed in February 2020 naming the founders, so copying is slow. Diagnostics use would add regulatory barriers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copycat found in sources opened. A market profile names Illumina, Grail and Exact Sciences as adjacent players; no dated evidence that they built the same wedge.

market_need_then: Methylation is a core signal for early cancer detection, and the Polsky Center article says currently available methylation measurement technologies have limits. Company claims a detection limit of 0.1 percent at one locus against 2 to 3 percent for current workflows (company stated).

identity.logo: Simple logo; not described in detail by sources
identity.visual_style: Clean layout with a bold all-caps headline and a partner call to action (company site)
identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific and direct; YC tagline is 'We engineer proteins that control the operating system of biology'

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand coverage found; name is easily confused with Epinomics and Epitome Therapeutics in search results.

outcome_analysis: Epinoma remains an early stage biotech tools company, still running clinical proof of concept work as of 2025 press. Its edge is a licensed methylation chemistry that is hard to copy, but no venture round is verifiable beyond a small seed reported by aggregators, so its trajectory is unclear. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news was found.
notes: Seed reported in October 2021 led by SeedtoB Capital with SeaX Ventures, Asymmetry Ventures, Y Combinator and George Church (aggregator snippets only; amounts range from $125K to $5M across aggregators; the VCA Online article returned 404). Not recorded as a round because no amount or primary source was verified. No competitors dated near the June 2021 batch were found in sources opened; the Polsky article names only unnamed 'major sequencing and diagnostic players'. Name origin not found; 'epi' likely refers to epigenetics but no source says so.
